title: Peek doesnt work when idle for a while
author: gabrielmulle
summary: Peek stops responding after PowerToys has been idle for an unspecified period, then works again after PowerToys is opened from the taskbar.

judgment.rationale: The report establishes a useful state transition but does not identify how long Peek must be idle, whether the failure affects all supported file types consistently, or what the Peek and PowerToys processes are doing when the hotkey is ignored. With no diagnostic archive, comment history, linked fix, or duplicate, a maintainer cannot distinguish a stalled Peek process, a background registration problem, or a lifecycle issue.
evidence: The issue targets Peek in PowerToys 0.101.2362 from the Microsoft Store.
Pressing Space does not open Peek for CSV, text, and Markdown files after PowerToys has been idle.
Opening PowerToys from its taskbar icon makes Peek work again.
The issue has no bug-report ZIP, comments, assignee, linked pull request, or visible linked issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the approximate idle duration, whether reopening the PowerToys Settings window is sufficient, and a fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after the hotkey failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix may apply to the Peek or runner lifecycle, but the idle interval and failing component are not identified and no existing fix is visible.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore Peek activation after prolonged idle
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unproven: a Peek or PowerToys background component may stop handling the Space activation after an idle or resume transition and become initialized again when the main PowerToys UI is opened.
plan: Capture the failure with the idle timing and lifecycle details, then use the diagnostic logs to identify whether Peek, the runner, or hotkey registration stops responding.
Trace the confirmed idle or resume path and restore the component's activation or registration without requiring the main PowerToys window to be opened.
Add regression coverage for activation after the confirmed idle or resume transition.
verification: Reproduce the original idle sequence and verify that Space opens Peek without opening PowerToys first.
Retest CSV, text, and Markdown files plus normal activation immediately after starting PowerToys.

confidence.rationale: The recovery after opening PowerToys supports a lifecycle hypothesis, but the report does not identify the idle transition, failing component, or diagnostic signature.

issue_context.summary: Peek does not respond to the Space hotkey after PowerToys remains idle, but opening PowerToys from the taskbar restores the behavior.
known_information: The affected PowerToys version is 0.101.2362 installed from the Microsoft Store.
The report names Peek and says the failure occurs with CSV, text, and Markdown files.
Opening PowerToys from the taskbar is followed by Peek working again.
No diagnostic ZIP, follow-up comment, assignee, linked fix, or visible duplicate is present.
inferences: The issue may involve a background Peek process, hotkey registration, or an idle/resume lifecycle transition rather than file-type parsing.
Opening the main PowerToys UI may reinitialize a component, but the report does not establish which component or whether Settings alone is sufficient.
issue_context.analysis: The recovery after opening PowerToys gives a reproducible before-and-after pattern, but the missing idle interval and diagnostics leave several lifecycle failure modes plausible. Collecting a fresh report immediately after the failure is more useful than proposing a file-specific fix.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, labels, assignees, comments, and visible timeline references.
Found no linked or mentioned upstream pull request or issue establishing an existing fix or duplicate.

information_gaps.information: The approximate idle duration before Peek stops responding, whether the failure occurs after sleep, lock, or display changes, and whether opening only PowerToys Settings restores Peek.
information_gaps.why_needed: These details distinguish a time-based background lifecycle problem from a resume, hotkey-registration, or full-application initialization problem.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the elapsed time and any sleep, lock, or display transition, then compare opening only Settings with opening the full PowerToys window.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured immediately after Space fails and before reopening PowerToys.
information_gaps.why_needed: Peek and runner logs may show whether the process is stopped, disconnected, or still receiving the activation request.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the failure, then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

actions.label: Request idle timing and diagnostics

comment.body: Thanks for reporting that Peek starts working again after you open PowerToys from the taskbar. Please share approximately how long PowerToys is idle before Space stops opening Peek, whether the failure follows sleep, locking, or a display change, and whether opening only the PowerToys Settings window restores it. Then reproduce the failure once more and add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward, before reopening PowerToys, so the logs capture the failing state.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
